work.title: Cadillac Ranch

facts.label: Enough: lugar certo
facts.sub: Com adjetivo, enough vem depois: old enough to drive. Com substantivo, vem antes: enough money. Na negativa, mostra falta: I don’t have enough practice.

facts.label: Adjetivo + enough
facts.sub: Com adjetivo, enough vem depois: old enough, careful enough, big enough. Para dizer a ação possível, acrescente to + verbo: He’s old enough to drive. Não diga enough old.

facts.label: Enough + substantivo
facts.sub: Com substantivo, enough vem antes: enough money, enough gas, enough room. Fica no sentido de quantidade suficiente: There’s enough room for four people.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “velho o bastante para dirigir” e “dinheiro suficiente”.
compare.us: Em inglês: adjetivo + enough (old enough); enough + substantivo (enough money). Diga old enough to drive.

items.s: Enough comes after a noun: money enough.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.

answers: Enough comes after an adjective. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Enough comes after a noun: money enough. → Falso (Say enough money.)
“Old enough to drive” is correct. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A hot gas station · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a hot Tuesday afternoon at a gas station in Austin. Trucks and cars wait at the pumps. Sue works at the counter and knows every customer. Rui comes in with a small bag of snacks. His old car stands outside with an empty tank. Sue asks about his gas.
“Hi, Rui! Do you have enough gas to get home?” says Sue. “Not really. I don’t have enough money for a full tank.” says Rui. “Ten dollars is enough to drive across town.” says Sue.
